title: Adaptive propagator for partial-header environments and SDK mismatches
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a low-overhead adaptive propagator that repairs and rewrites incomplete or truncated trace/carrier headers produced by older or constrained SDKs and by intermediate proxies (mobile networks, CDNs). The goal is to improve cross-service trace correlation without requiring coordinated SDK upgrades. Work spans SDK middleware (repair/wrap), inbound gateway logic (reconstruction heuristics), and tests/metrics to detect regressions.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end traces for requests with truncated or split headers are matched at least 95% more often than baseline for test corpus of mobile/CDN edge traces.
New SDK middleware adds <200ns median allocation overhead on fastpath and is optional by feature flag.
Gateway reconstruction has configurable fallback strategies: byte-reassembly, id-fingerprint mapping, and safe-id-generation — default config yields no PII leakage.
Unit and integration tests cover header-split, truncated-baggage, and missing-sampling cases with golden trace expectations.
New observability metrics emitted: propagation.rewrites_total, propagation.rewrites_by_strategy, propagation.rewrite_latency_ms, and propagation.unreconstructable_total.
PR reviewed by runtime and sdk teams and merged; e2e job green on staging for two days.
No change to production sampling behavior unless feature flag enabled for a customer; rollout docs written in Console runbook.
technical_notes: Design uses a three-tier approach: 1) SDK middleware fastpath that preserves original headers and emits lightweight provenance stamp; 2) edge/gateway reconstruction that attempts assembly using sequence markers and compact checksums; 3) conservative id-fingerprint mapping when assembly fails, using per-tenant namespace to avoid cross-tenant collisions. Sampling alignment uses a deterministic hash of reconstructed id + tenant salt to decide local sampling hints. All heuristics are opt-in and logged as metrics and events.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Reconstruction heuristics can produce false-positives — mitigate via namespace salt and conservative collision thresholds.
Extra header parsing at gateways increases CPU on high-throughput paths; mitigate with rate-limited sampling of rewrite attempts and fastpath skip for trusted internal sources.
Privacy: avoid storing raw header payloads and strip potential PII before any persisted logs; default mode emits only checksums and strategy labels.
Compatibility: older SDKs that already mutate carriers require per-language adaptations; prioritize Go/Node/Java first.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype gateway reconstruction library (Go) and unit tests against captured truncated-header corpus.
Week 2: Implement SDK middleware in Node and Go with runtime feature-flag and light provenance header.
Week 3: Integrate metrics emission and dashboard (Console) tiles for rewrite rates and failures.
Week 4: End-to-end integration, perf tuning, and rollout gating with staged customers.
Post-release: Add Java SDK support and automatic opt-in rules for dedicated customers.
